diagnosis.missing_function: Triggered wake-up (passive tuned trigger beam + comparator, module A); no combination of the allowed C_uF and poll_ms variables can replace it.
diagnosis.reason:
With the module set fixed OFF, acquisition must be done by polling, which creates an unsatisfiable conflict:
- Burst capture needs the polling cycle to fit inside the event: capture = event_ms/(poll_ms + 62.5) - 1 >= 0  =>  poll_ms <= 87.5 ms.
- Energy needs the polling duty cycle low enough: demand = 0.003*min(1, 62.5/poll_ms) <= net = power - idle ≈ 119.9 - 1.4 = 118.5 uW  =>  poll_ms >= ~1580 ms (and poll_ms < 62.5 ms only makes demand the full 3000 uW).
These two requirements are mutually exclusive, so no C_uF/poll_ms choice can pass. C_uF cannot help: harvested power, idle, and capture all depend only on R/h/mass/modules and poll_ms, and C only trades cold_charge/burst_energy/area. A large C can satisfy burst_energy (needs C_uF > ~113) but that does not touch the capture-vs-energy deadlock.

The physics intentionally provides the fix: the passive trigger beam (L2=18 mm, m2=0.14 g) resonates at ~210.6 Hz, matching the 210 Hz event, and module A has only 0.5 uW idle. With A installed, active capture = env/trigger_V - 1 (positive at ~0.5 g event) and active demand = packet/event_period ≈ 50 uW < net ≈ 118 uW, so energy, capture, cold_charge, burst (at C_uF≈150), stress, area and rectifier all pass simultaneously. Module B is not viable (180 uW idle makes net negative); C and D are unnecessary. But module A cannot be installed through the allowed-variable interface (attempt returned 'Outside declared domain'), so the design cannot satisfy every constraint from the current all-off module set. Missing capability: a triggered wake-up (module A).

diagnosis.missing_function: Low-power event-triggered wake/acquisition using module A (passive tuned trigger beam + comparator)
diagnosis.reason: With A/B inactive, polling must satisfy poll_ms + 62.5 <= 150 ms, i.e. poll_ms <= 87.5 ms, to capture the event. At poll_ms=87, energy fails for C=50, 75, 200, and 500 uF, so storage sizing cannot fix it. Relaxing polling to 4000 ms clears the energy violation but changes the worst violation to capture. Thus the design cannot meet both energy and capture with only C_uF and poll_ms; it needs a low-idle wake path. Module A is the appropriate minimal addition (idle 0.5 uW). Module B is not justified because its 180 uW idle is excessive for this low-power node, and C/D do not address the polling/capture conflict.

diagnosis.missing_function: triggered wake/acquisition path (preferably module A) with polling disabled
diagnosis.reason: With only C_uF and poll_ms adjustable and A/B uninstalled, the capture and energy constraints are mutually exclusive. Guaranteed event capture requires poll_ms + 62.5 <= 150 ms, i.e. poll_ms <= 87.5 ms. But at the current poll_ms=100 ms the node already needs ~1876 uW while harvesting only ~120 uW; reducing poll_ms further only increases polling energy. Raising poll_ms enough to make average energy positive would miss the 150-ms event. C_uF affects burst/cold-charge storage, not average polling energy. Therefore the missing function is a triggered acquisition/wake path that replaces continuous polling. Module A (0.5 uW idle) is the viable choice; B's 180 uW idle exceeds the available harvest. With A installed, storage would also need increasing to about 150 uF for burst energy, but module installation is not exposed by the allowed changes.

diagnosis.missing_function: Harvester/rectifier operating-point tuning (R_kohm, h, mass_g, gate_V), plus a triggered wake-up path if polling is removed
diagnosis.reason: With only C_uF and poll_ms adjustable, capture can be made to pass at poll_ms=87.5 ms, but energy remains infeasible: required average power is ~2144 uW versus ~42.3 uW harvested (energy slack -21.02). Increasing poll_ms reduces demand but necessarily violates the 150 ms capture window; C_uF cannot raise steady harvested power. Rectifier voltage also remains 0.244 below its threshold (2.419 V versus required 3.2 V), and burst-energy slack is still negative. These require changing the harvester/rectifier operating point or adding/replacing polling with a triggered acquisition path, neither of which is available under the allowed variables.

diagnosis.missing_function: Triggered wake-up/acquisition (passive tuned trigger A) plus rectifier/startup tuning (gate_V or harvester load/tuning)
diagnosis.reason: With only C_uF and poll_ms actionable, no feasible point exists. Without A/B, capture requires poll_ms+62.5 <= 150 ms, i.e. poll_ms <= 87.5 ms, whose polling energy is far above the 42.27 uW harvested. Even at the maximum poll_ms=4000, energy is still short (required 48.275 uW vs harvested 42.266 uW), and capture fails. Independently, rectifier_voltage slack remains -0.244 for both C=75 uF and C=1500 uF, since the rectified background is about 2.419-0.3=2.119 V, below gate_V=2.9 V. A low-idle passive trigger module A is the appropriate functional addition to replace polling; B costs 180 uW idle, exceeding harvest, and C/D do not solve startup or capture. Module installation and gate/harvester retuning are outside the exposed action domain, so the current design cannot satisfy all constraints.

diagnosis.missing_function: Impact stress reduction independent of the rectifier load (a voltage-triggered shunt such as module D, or harvester mechanical retuning of h/mass).
diagnosis.reason: With only C_uF and R_kohm adjustable, burst energy and rectifier voltage can be met, but impact stress cannot. At R=50 kΩ and C=130 µF, burst_energy=+0.134 and rectifier_voltage=+0.005, yet stress=350.8 MPa versus a 285 MPa limit (slack -0.231). Lowering R to 20 kΩ worsens stress to 380.8 MPa and fails rectifier voltage; raising R to 60-100 kΩ also leaves stress at 352-369 MPa. Storage capacitance does not affect steady-state impact stress. The design therefore needs a high-voltage event-only stress limiter—module D—or mechanical retuning not exposed in the allowed variables.

diagnosis.missing_function: High-voltage shunt damping / stress limiting (module D), or mechanical stress relief via the harvester beam/tip-mass variables
diagnosis.reason: Using only the allowed C_uF and R_kohm variables, all constraints except stress can be satisfied. Best explored point (C=150 uF, R=50 kΩ) has energy slack +0.158, cold-charge +9.44 s, burst +0.306, capture +40.88, rectifier +0.005, area +0.742, and acquisition +1.0, but stress is 350.8 MPa versus the 285 MPa limit (slack -0.231). Sweeping R over 20, 45, 50, 60, and 100 kΩ gives a shallow minimum near 350 MPa, still far above the limit; changing C does not affect stress. Therefore the design is infeasible without a high-voltage damping/shunt function such as module D, or without changing the disallowed mechanical variables (h or mass).

diagnosis.missing_function: Mechanical stress reduction (lower harvester thickness h or tip mass) or a voltage-triggered shunt clamp (module D); C_uF and R_kohm alone cannot satisfy the 225 MPa stress limit.
diagnosis.reason: With C_uF=150 and R_kohm=60, burst energy and rectifier voltage pass, but stress remains ~352 MPa versus the 225 MPa limit. Sweeping R_kohm shows the stress floor is ~351 MPa near the near-resonant load (R~45–50 kΩ); detuning the load only increases stress. Storage capacitance does not affect mechanical stress. Therefore no feasible C/R setting exists under the allowed variables; stress must be reduced mechanically or clamped by an additional shunt.

diagnosis.missing_function: D (voltage-triggered parallel resistive shunt) for event stress damping
diagnosis.reason: Across C_uF 75–1500 and R_kohm 2–300 (including near piezoelectric impedance match), the evaluator still reports stress as the worst violated constraint. Storage and rectifier-load tuning cannot resolve it; the design lacks an installed high-voltage damping/shunt path. Module D is the available function intended to reduce peak stress, though it may sacrifice harvested power. Mechanical de-rating (h/mass/beam) would be an alternative but is outside the allowed C/R variables.
